description: Dashboard command center with real data + actionable recommendations, Analytics, the 'What Should I Do Next?' seller assistant (mock, behind an interface), and Import/Export (P0 item 2; P1 item 20; sections 5,27,28,35,45). Replace the placeholder dashboard with real KPIs (Total/Unlisted/Listed inventory value, Estimated Profit, Cards in Inventory, Cards Sold, Revenue, Pending Orders) each with supporting context; the 'What Needs Your Attention?' section (valuable cards unlisted, underpriced listings, orders to fulfill, bulk ready to package, missing storage locations); a 'List These Next' recommendation engine; an Inventory Value chart (total/listed/unlisted/bulk) as hand-drawn SVG; and Recent Activity. Analytics page with revenue/profit/cards sold/avg sale price/avg profit per card/inventory turnover/days to sale/best sets/best Pokemon/best rarities/bulk vs singles revenue as clean SVG charts. A modular SellerAssistant (mock) that answers natural-language questions from the user's actual data. CSV import/export.
steps: Reminder: zero deps, `unset NODE_OPTIONS`. This is the final integrating feature: depends on FEAT-001..007 (all repos, pricing/classification, listings, orders/sales/expenses, bulk). Read the repositories + services before starting. All aggregates are computed with SQL over node:sqlite; charts are hand-drawn inline SVG (no chart library, no deps).

src/services/dashboardService.ts: compute KPIs from repos scoped to the user (section 5): totalInventoryValue (sum market_value*qty), unlistedInventoryValue (status not Listed/Sold), listedInventoryValue, estimatedProfit (from sales net + projected net on unsold via pricing), cardsInInventory, cardsSold, revenue (sum sales.sale_price), pendingOrders (orders not Delivered/Cancelled). Each returns value + supporting context string (e.g. unlisted -> '173 cards waiting to be listed').

src/services/attentionService.ts (section 5A, 45): produce actionable items: N valuable cards unlisted (value over a threshold, status not Listed), N listings underpriced (listing price < suggested from pricing engine) / overpriced, N orders needing fulfillment (status New/Picking/Packed), N bulk cards ready to package (available bulk count -> approx lots), N cards missing storage locations. Each item has a count, message, and a link to the relevant filtered page.

src/services/recommendationService.ts (section 5B): 'List These Next' - rank unlisted inventory by a priority score combining estimated value, demand proxy (inverse competition / recent sold volume from price snapshots), competition, profit potential (net after fees), and time sitting in inventory (age since date_acquired). Return the top N cards with the score rationale. Reuse pricing/classification services.

src/services/analyticsService.ts (section 27): aggregate revenue, profit, cards sold, avg sale price, avg profit/card, inventory turnover, days-to-sale (avg date_sold - date_acquired), best-performing sets/Pokemon/rarities (group sales by joined card fields), bulk vs singles revenue. Return series suitable for charts.

src/views/components/charts.ts: pure functions returning inline SVG strings - barChart, lineChart/areaChart (for inventory value breakdown + revenue over time), and a small donut/stacked bar for singles vs bulk. No external libs. Accessible (title/labels), responsive via viewBox.

src/views/pages/dashboard.ts: rebuild the real Dashboard - KPI cards row (section 5 metrics with context), the highly-visible 'What Needs Your Attention?' panel (actionable cards with counts + links), 'List These Next' list, the Inventory Value chart (total/listed/unlisted/bulk), and Recent Activity (recent scans, listings created, cards sold, orders shipped, inventory changes - a merged recent-events feed). Every major screen should surface 'here's what to do next' (section 45).
src/views/pages/analytics.ts + route GET /analytics: professional analytics dashboard using the SVG charts + summary stat cards for all section-27 metrics; clean, uncluttered (section 31).

src/services/interfaces/sellerAssistant.ts + src/services/mock/mockSellerAssistant.ts (section 28,38): SellerAssistant.ask(userId, question): Promise<{answer, data?}>. The mock parses intent from keywords (list today / sitting too long / most valuable unlisted / singles vs bulk / how much in boxes / which set makes the most money) and answers using REAL aggregates from the repos/services (not canned text) - e.g. 'most valuable unlisted' returns top cards from recommendationService; 'which set makes the most' from analyticsService. Document that a real LLM implements the same interface without UI change. Add a small assistant UI on the Dashboard (a question box with suggested prompts) + route POST /api/assistant {question}.

src/services/importExport.ts + routes (section 35): Export - GET /export/inventory.csv, /export/sales.csv, /export/profit-report.csv, /export/listings.csv streaming CSV from repos. Import - POST /api/import/inventory accepting a CSV (parse with a small pure CSV parser, no deps) to bulk-create inventory/cards, with validation + a summary of created/skipped/errored rows (never lose data on bad rows - report them). Add an Import/Export area (Settings or Inventory toolbar).
Wire Dashboard (/ and /dashboard), Analytics nav, and the assistant. Ensure the demo seed data makes all of these panels populated and non-empty.

Tests (node:test): src/services/dashboardService.test.ts - KPIs computed correctly over a seeded temp DB (unlisted value excludes Listed/Sold; revenue sums sales; pending orders count). src/services/attentionService.test.ts - detects unlisted valuable cards, underpriced listings, orders needing fulfillment, missing storage. src/services/recommendationService.test.ts - ranking orders higher-value/higher-demand/older items above low-value fresh ones. src/services/analyticsService.test.ts - aggregates (revenue, avg sale price, best set, singles vs bulk) match hand-computed expectations. src/services/mockSellerAssistant.test.ts - 'most valuable unlisted' and 'which set makes the most money' return data-driven answers from the seeded DB. src/services/importExport.test.ts - CSV export round-trips through import (export then import yields matching rows) and bad rows are reported without aborting the whole import.
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build` and `npm test` pass including dashboard, attention, recommendation, analytics, assistant, and import/export tests.

The Dashboard shows real KPIs with supporting context, a prominent 'What Needs Your Attention?' section, a 'List These Next' list, an Inventory Value chart (total/listed/unlisted/bulk), and Recent Activity - all populated from the seeded demo data.

The Analytics page renders clean SVG charts + stats for the section-27 metrics (revenue, profit, cards sold, avg sale price, avg profit/card, turnover, days to sale, best sets/Pokemon/rarities, bulk vs singles).
The seller assistant answers questions like 'what's my most valuable unlisted inventory?' and 'which set is making me the most money?' using real inventory/sales data, behind a swappable interface.
CSV export produces inventory/sales/profit/listing reports and CSV import bulk-creates inventory with per-row validation and an error summary (bad rows do not abort the import).
